description: Lint the portable copy of each published skill in the mifunedev/skills registry so it never names a path or a slash command an installer will not have. Issue #758 Option C. Ships a linter, a reviewer-facing contract that doubles as the machine-readable exception list, a CI-enforced test suite that verifies the check by rejection, an opt-in probe, a publishing step that gives the check a caller, and a one-time sweep that reports findings without fixing them.
revision: post-critique. Two adversarial critics ran before implementation; see critique.md for the adjudication of all 19 findings.

userStories.title: Ship the portability linter
userStories.description: As a maintainer publishing a skill, I want a check that reads the portable copy on its own and reports every reference an installer cannot resolve, so that the class of defect caught by hand in mifunedev/skills#7 is caught by a command instead.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/scripts/registry-portability.sh` exists and is executable.
The script sets `set -euo pipefail`.
The script accepts `--registry <dir>` naming a checkout of the published registry, `--allow <file>` overriding the exceptions source, and `--strict-exceptions`.
The script discovers skill folders by scanning `<dir>/skills/` and hardcodes no skill name.
The script reads every `*.md` and `*.sh` file under each discovered skill folder.
Rule `OH-PATH` reports any `.oh/` path reference in a scanned file.

Rule `HARNESS-SKILL` reads the first whitespace-delimited token inside a backticked span; when that token starts with `/` and the remainder names no folder under `<dir>/skills/`, it is reported. An invocation carrying arguments, such as a backticked `/name <arg>`, is therefore read.
Rule `HARNESS-SKILL` does not report Unix filesystem roots: bin, boot, dev, etc, home, lib, media, mnt, opt, proc, root, run, sbin, srv, sys, tmp, usr, var.
Rule `HARNESS-SKILL` does not report metasyntactic placeholders whose name starts with foo, bar, baz, or qux.
Rule `DANGLING-REF` reports a backticked span that begins with `references/<f>.md` or `scripts/<f>.sh` when that file does not exist under the skill folder being scanned.
Rule `DANGLING-REF` does not report a path that rule `OH-PATH` already reported on the same line, so a `.oh/` path is never counted twice.
Each finding is printed as `<path>:<line>: <RULE-ID> <token>` where `<path>` is relative to the registry root.
Findings are printed in a deterministic order, sorted by path, then line, then rule id, then token, so two runs over the same tree produce byte-identical output.
Each finding also prints a paste-ready exception stub carrying the class placeholder, rule id, registry-relative path, and line hash.
An exception entry is keyed on the tuple of registry-relative path, rule id, and the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the trimmed source line.
An exception entry is classified `ALLOW` or `KNOWN`.
`ALLOW` suppresses the finding. `KNOWN` does not suppress the finding and does not change the exit code; it labels the finding as already triaged.
The run prints the counts of findings suppressed by `ALLOW`, findings labelled `KNOWN`, and findings that are neither.

An exception entry whose hash occurs nowhere in the single file it names is reported as stale. Stale entries warn and do not change the exit code unless `--strict-exceptions` is passed, in which case the script exits 1.
Staleness is evaluated only against the file the entry names, never against the whole tree.
The script prints the number of skill folders and files it scanned on every run, including a clean run.
The script exits 0 only when every finding was suppressed by an `ALLOW` entry.
The script exits 1 when any finding survives, whether that finding is labelled `KNOWN` or is new.
The script exits 2 when `--registry` is absent, names a missing directory, names a directory with no `skills/` subdirectory, or names a `skills/` subdirectory holding no skill folder.
The script exits 2 when the total scanned-file count is zero.
The script exits 2 when the exceptions file is missing or contains no fenced block tagged `allow`, rather than treating an unreadable exception list as an empty one.
The script accepts a present-but-empty `allow` block as a valid zero-exception configuration and does not exit 2 for it.

The script collects targets and findings without `mapfile` over a process substitution whose command may fail, and without appending to an array inside a piped `while read` subshell, because both lose the failure under `set -euo pipefail`.
The script writes to no file under the registry it scans.
The script's own output contains none of the retired audit vocabulary tokens guarded by `.oh/evals/probes/audit-stale-references.sh`, so evidence may quote it verbatim.
`bash -n .oh/scripts/registry-portability.sh` reports no syntax error.
`shellcheck -S warning .oh/scripts/registry-portability.sh` reports no finding, because the CI shellcheck glob covers `.oh/scripts/*.sh`.

userStories.title: Write the harness-to-registry contract and the exception list as one artifact
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want the intended deltas between the canonical skill and its portable copy written down in the same file the checker reads, so that the documentation cannot drift away from the enforced behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/scripts/registry-portability.md` exists.
The file sits under `.oh/scripts/` rather than `.oh/docs/` because `.oh/manifest.json` ships `scripts/**` and excludes `docs/**`, and the document states that reason.
`.oh/docs/README.md` gains an index entry pointing at it.
The document states the canonical path `.oh/skills/<name>/` and the published path `skills/<name>/`, and names the registry repository and its base branch.

The document records the intended harness-to-registry deltas for the `ste` skill: invocation paths become relative, harness-specific sections are generalized or made conditional, and the registry copy adds a LICENSE file.
The document states all three rules, `OH-PATH`, `HARNESS-SKILL`, and `DANGLING-REF`, including the backtick requirement and both suppression sets.
The document shows the command that runs the check against a registry checkout, and names the environment variable the probe reads.
The document explains how to add an exception, including how to obtain the line hash from the paste-ready stub the linter prints.
The document contains exactly one fenced block tagged `allow`.
Every non-comment, non-blank line inside the `allow` block has five `|`-separated fields: class, rule id, registry-relative path, line hash, reason.
The class field is `ALLOW` for an intentional and correct reference, or `KNOWN` for a real finding reported and left unrepaired.
Every exception entry carries a non-empty reason, and no reason contains a `|` character.
Every `ALLOW` reason states why the unreachable reference is nonetheless safe for an installer.
Every `KNOWN` reason states why the finding was not repaired by this change.
The `allow` block reproduces the measured day-one state: 8 `ALLOW` entries and 5 `KNOWN` entries against registry master `1d11ab6`.

The document states the limitations without softening them: `HARNESS-SKILL` reads backticked single-word tokens only; `OH-PATH` covers `.oh/` only while the registry carries 79 `.claude/` references across 15 of its 18 skills; a client built-in command is indistinguishable from a missing registry skill; and `template/` is not scanned.
The document states that the registry has no CI workflow, so this check gates publishing from the harness side and cannot block a commit made directly against the registry.
The document states that an exception is not a repair and points at the sweep report for findings left unfixed.
The document contains none of the retired audit vocabulary tokens guarded by `.oh/evals/probes/audit-stale-references.sh`.

userStories.title: Verify the check by rejection under CI
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want the guard proven by feeding it input it must reject, so that a green run is evidence the check works rather than evidence it ran.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/scripts/__tests__/registry-portability.test.ts` exists and runs under `pnpm test`.
The suite invokes the real script through `spawnSync`, matching the house pattern in `.oh/scripts/__tests__/check-pnpm-pin.test.ts`, and mocks no part of it.
The suite builds its fixtures in a temporary directory and never depends on a network fetch or a registry clone.
A clean fixture registry produces exit code 0.
A fixture whose portable copy reintroduces a `.oh/` reference produces exit code 1, and the output names the offending file and the offending line number.
A fixture whose portable copy names a backticked slash command absent from the fixture registry produces exit code 1, and the output names the offending file and the offending line number.
A fixture naming a backticked slash command that carries arguments is reported, so the rule is not defeated by an argument.
A fixture reference that resolves to a skill folder present in the fixture registry produces no finding.
A fixture citing `references/<f>.md` absent from its own skill folder produces exit code 1 under rule `DANGLING-REF`, and one that is present produces no finding.
A `.oh/` path is reported once, by `OH-PATH` only, and never also by `DANGLING-REF`.
A finding suppressed by an `ALLOW` entry produces exit code 0, and deleting that entry makes the same fixture exit 1.
Editing the suppressed line so its hash changes makes the previously suppressed fixture exit 1, proving the exception cannot outlive the line it excuses.
A `KNOWN` entry does not suppress: the fixture still exits 1, and the finding is labelled as triaged in the output.
An exception entry whose hash matches nothing in the file it names is reported as stale, exits 0 by default, and exits 1 under `--strict-exceptions`.
An exception entry matching a line in a different file does not suppress the finding, because staleness and suppression are both scoped to the named file.
Pointing the script at a missing directory produces exit code 2.
Pointing the script at a directory with no `skills/` subdirectory produces exit code 2.
Pointing the script at a `skills/` subdirectory holding no skill folder produces exit code 2, not 0.
Pointing the script at a registry whose skill folders hold no `*.md` or `*.sh` file produces exit code 2, not 0.
Pointing the script at a missing exceptions file produces exit code 2.
An exceptions file whose `allow` block is absent produces exit code 2, and one whose `allow` block is present but empty produces a normal run.

A fixture reproducing the three historical defects of registry commit `036a53f` produces exit code 1 and reports all three, so the proof survives deletion of the upstream branch that commit is reachable from.
Two runs over the same fixture produce byte-identical output.

The suite asserts that the shipped `.oh/scripts/registry-portability.md` parses: exactly one `allow` block, every entry has five fields, every class is `ALLOW` or `KNOWN`, every hash is 12 hex characters, and every reason is non-empty and contains no `|`.
`pnpm test` passes with the suite present, and the pre-existing 481 tests still pass.

userStories.title: Expose the check as an opt-in probe
userStories.description: As the harness operator, I want the check available to the probe suite against a real registry checkout, without adding a network dependency to the default run.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/evals/probes/registry-portability.sh` exists and is executable.
The probe begins with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` followed by `# tier:`, `# source:`, and `# desc:` header lines.
The probe exits 2 with a SKIPPED message when no registry checkout is supplied through its documented environment variable.
The probe exits 2 with a SKIPPED message when the supplied path is not a registry checkout.
The probe exits 1 with a REGRESSION message when the linter reports a surviving finding, and relays the linter output.
The probe exits 0 with a PASS message when the linter reports no surviving finding.
The probe exits 2 rather than 0 when the linter itself exits 2, so a broken invocation is never recorded as a pass.
The probe does not pass `--strict-exceptions`, so a stale exception entry is not reported as a regression.
`bash -n .oh/evals/probes/registry-portability.sh` reports no syntax error.
Running `bash .oh/evals/probes/registry-portability.sh` with no registry supplied exits 2.
`bash .oh/skills/eval/run.sh` still exits 0 with the probe present and no registry configured.

userStories.title: Sweep the registry once and report the findings
userStories.description: As the issue author, I want every skill already in the registry checked once and the results written down, so that the pre-existing state is known instead of assumed clean. The sweep reports; it does not repair.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/tasks/registry-drift-lint/sweep.md` exists.
The report records the registry commit that was swept and the exact command that produced the result.
The report states the total number of skill folders scanned and confirms the scan covered all of them, and enumerates by name only the folders that produced a finding.
The report reconciles the issue's count of 17 pre-existing skills with the 18 folders present: 17 plus `ste`.
The report lists every finding with its rule id, file, and line.
The report separates entries classified `ALLOW` from findings classified `KNOWN`.
Each `KNOWN` finding records why it was not repaired here.
The report states explicitly that no file in `mifunedev/skills` was modified by this change.
The working tree of the registry checkout is unmodified after the sweep, and the report records the observed evidence for that.
The report records that the registry side is deliberately left unpointed at this contract, and why.
The report records the `.claude/` reference count as a measured follow-up rather than a repaired finding.
The report contains none of the retired audit vocabulary tokens guarded by `.oh/evals/probes/audit-stale-references.sh`.
`bash .oh/evals/probes/audit-stale-references.sh` exits 0 after every task artifact has been force-added to the branch.

userStories.title: Prove the check against the real historical defects
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want the check run against the actual registry tree that carried the three defects, using the exception list that actually ships, so that the proof is a real regression rather than a fixture written to match the implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: The pre-fix tree is extracted read-only with `git archive <commit> | tar -x`, so the registry checkout the brief forbids modifying is never written to.
The linter is run against registry commit `036a53f`, the state one commit before the manual repair.
The run uses the shipped `.oh/scripts/registry-portability.md`, not an emptied or weakened exception list.
The run exits 1.
The output names `skills/ste/SKILL.md` line 102 for the `/caveman` claim.
The output names `skills/ste/references/rules.md` line 420 for the `/caveman` example.
The output names `skills/ste/SKILL.md` line 285 for the `.oh/skills/retro/references/memory-protocol.md` pointer.
The linter is run against the current registry master and its exit code and findings are recorded.
The two runs demonstrate that the exception accepting the repaired pointer at master line 282 does not suppress the defect at line 285, and the differing line hashes are recorded as the reason.
Both runs, their exact commands, and their real output are recorded in `.oh/tasks/registry-drift-lint/evidence.md`.
No claim in the evidence document is predicted or reconstructed output.

userStories.title: Give the check a caller in the publishing procedure
userStories.description: As the issue author, I want the check named in the procedure a skill author already follows, so that publishing the next skill runs it instead of relying on someone remembering it exists.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/builder/references/skill.md` gains a step covering publication to the registry.
The step names `bash .oh/scripts/registry-portability.sh --registry <dir>` as a required gate before a registry pull request is opened.
The step points at `.oh/scripts/registry-portability.md` for the rules and the exception procedure.
The step states that the registry has no CI, so this gate is the only automated check on the portable copy.
The added text contains none of the retired audit vocabulary tokens guarded by `.oh/evals/probes/audit-stale-references.sh`.
No existing instruction in that file is removed or contradicted.
`bash .oh/skills/eval/run.sh` still exits 0 after the edit.
